text.p: One of disgraced rogue trader Nick Leeson's former bosses at Barings is demanding a 500,000 pound ($789,000) performance bonus, 20 months after the British investment bank collapsed in a mountain of debts.

Mary Walz, an American, told a London industrial tribunal on Monday that Barings, now owned by Dutch company Internationale Nederlanden Group (ING), operated a profit-related bonus scheme for high-flying staff.
But the day after Barings executives allegedly promised Walz her bonus, the bank ran into crisis over huge losses run up by Singapore-based trader Leeson.

Walz, the bank's Global Head of Equity Financial Products, which involve short term derivatives, claims she was told by her chairman when he announced the award on February 23 last year: "You are a star."
She insists the promise was effectively "made in stone" but Barings said the profit-related scheme became non-existent when all its profits disappeared because of Leeson.

Barings was brought down in February 1995 by Leeson's unauthorised derivatives trading losses of nearly $1.4 billion. ING stepped in and bought the bank, paying bonuses to those employees it retained.
Walz, who was not retained by ING, was criticised in a Barings Bank report and her former bosses suggested that incompetence could result in her being in breach of contract.

The hearing was told that Walz was an expert in Far East banking and was responsible for setting up a successful operation in Hong Kong, which made millions. Leeson, based in Singapore, also came under her derivatives operation.
He is serving a six-and-half year jail sentence in Singapore for fraud after his market dealings led to the bank's collapse.
